key_insight: CAIRN extends 3D scene understanding from single rooms to realistic multi-room homes by making the model aware of scene topology, so it can reason over both object-level and room-level relationships. In simple terms, it helps a 3D multimodal model understand how spaces connect, not just what objects are present.
problem_solved: Most existing 3D-LLMs are limited to simplified single-room scenes and struggle with household environments made of multiple connected rooms, diverse objects, and hierarchical spatial relationships.
method: Introduces a topology-aware 3D-LLM designed for cross-room scene understanding in multi-room environments.
Aligns transformer attention with the scene hierarchy to explicitly model object-level relations and room-level connectivity.
Uses structured spatial reasoning so the model can answer questions grounded in realistic household layouts rather than isolated rooms.
impact: This work pushes 3D multimodal AI closer to real-world deployment in homes, robotics, and embodied assistants, where understanding connected spaces is essential. For practitioners, it offers a blueprint for adding topology and hierarchy to improve spatial reasoning beyond single-room benchmarks.
visual_elements: A floor-plan style diagram showing multiple connected rooms with objects and room boundaries
A hierarchy graphic illustrating object-level, room-level, and house-level relationships
An attention map overlay demonstrating how the model links entities across rooms
A before-vs-after comparison of single-room 3D-LLMs versus CAIRN in multi-room reasoning
paper_title: CAIRN: Cross-Room 3D Scene Understanding with Topology-Aware Large Multimodal Models
paper_authors: He Liang, Chenyang Ma, Yiming Zhang, Sangyun Shin, Andrew Markham
